Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{6}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{6}^{-6}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{6}(3x-9f(x))\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{-6}^{6}x\,\text{d}x\,-\,9{\int }_{-6}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{-6}^{6}\,-\,9(-1) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{{6}^{2}-(-6)^{2}}{2}\,+\,9 \\  & =3\cdot 0\,+\,9 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
